directive:
Literature-first finding for oeq:multi-district-frontier: DO NOT infer global paired SCM families from a local FACE_NOT_IDENTIFIED witness under the current definitions. The cited completeness constructions do not discharge that implication. Precise gap: the local test only yields q_D^± ∈ K_D(m_D); globally one only knows π_D(C(P)) ⊆ K_D(m_D). Reverse inclusion/product-face surjectivity is exactly unproved, because complete multi-district menu cells impose polynomial sum-product equalities that K_D omits whenever extraction fails. Thus local variation can be spurious relative to the global fiber; it lifts iff the relevant points lie in π_D(C(P)), and opposite ranking requires global gap extrema L<0<U (failure of one strict dominance certificate alone is weaker).

PRIMARY RECEIPTS. Correa–Lee–Bareinboim 2022 PMLR PDF https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/correa22a/correa22a.pdf: p3 assumes finite domains/recursive SCM; p5 defines available data as complete observational/interventional laws P^i(V;σ_Z), not Layer-3 menus; p6 Lemma 3.1 transports a ctf-factor only when none of its variables is selected and Eq.(14) factorizes into c-components; pp19–20 Lemma B.1/Theorem 5.1 obtain failure witnesses through σ-TR. Crucially pp11–12, Lemma A.1 explicitly replaces A2’s observed domain by X_A2×{0,1}; therefore its necessity construction is not a fixed-original-alphabet theorem.
Raghavan–Bareinboim 2026 arXiv v2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23541, source TR_app_proofs.tex: lines 39–42 ctf-factor product/decomposition; 56–71 one-hedge binary parity witness; 85–96 ctf-thicket combines a hedges using an a-bit variable; 102–128 Step-vii global input preservation explicitly makes every observable an (a′+1)-bit encoding, matches all one-specification input distributions, and changes target. This is one SCM specification, has no source labels/district-invariance equations, and enlarges observed alphabets.
Zhang–Tian–Bareinboim 2022, arXiv:2110.05690 / PMLR https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/zhang22ab/zhang22ab.pdf: p3 Theorem 2.4 (source section3.tex lines 52–66) gives counterfactual equivalence to finite canonical SCMs while preserving the observed domains/graph; lines 73–89 give finite recursive polynomial evaluation; p5 Eq.(9)/Theorem 2.8 gives sharp extrema by imposing all supplied distribution-cell equalities. Appendix A source lines 299–308 factors canonical-partition probabilities over c-components; lines 445–454 canonicalizes each c-component while preserving all counterfactual laws. This supports a GLOBAL polynomial-fiber theorem, not local-face surjectivity.

Scope only oeq:multi-district-frontier. Do not claim that FACE_NOT_IDENTIFIED or failure of a strict arm-order dual certificate produces global countermodels. Replace the question by the strongest unconditional same-topic theorem: define the exact finite canonical global fiber Θ(P) using one Zhang–Tian–Bareinboim canonical SCM parameter block for every source domain; impose (i) the current graph/recursive and district-factorization restrictions, (ii) equality of induced district response-map laws q_D^s=q_D^⋆ exactly for D∩Δ_s=∅, and (iii) for every supplied source-labelled regime and every cell of its complete law, the exact recursive polynomial equality Φ_{s,a,v}(θ)=P_a^s(v). Prove Θ(P) is nonempty and compact, preserves the declared observed alphabets X, and is counterfactually equivalent to C(P) for all supplied cells and target cells. For a target cell T (or the common-evidence numerator gap G_{ρ,σ}), define L=min_{θ∈Θ(P)}T(θ), U=max_{θ∈Θ(P)}T(θ); extrema are attained. Prove identification iff L=U; if L<U, minimizer and maximizer yield two original-observed-alphabet compatible SCM families agreeing on every complete supplied menu law and differing on T. For arm order with common evidence positive throughout Θ(P), prove uniform σ>ρ iff min G>0, uniform ρ>σ iff max G<0, and opposite strict rankings iff min G<0<max G. State explicitly that a local q_D witness lifts only when it belongs to π_DΘ(P), and that π_DΘ(P)⊆K_D(m_D) is all currently justified; equality is available only from thm:one-district-fiber-projection. Do not cite CTFTR or CTFIDU+ as proving the reverse inclusion: CTFTR has only Layer-1/2 inputs and its countermodel proof may enlarge observed domains, while the CTFIDU+ thicket construction is one-specification and explicitly uses multi-bit observed encodings. Use Zhang–Tian–Bareinboim canonicalization solely to prove the exact global polynomial optimization frontier. Preserve oeq:multi-district-frontier as unresolved only if the solver cannot formalize this global canonical fiber without adding assumptions.

This cleanly distinguishes local relaxation witnesses from global compatible-family witnesses and avoids laundering the gluing crux.

directive:
D0 MAXIMALITY CHECKPOINT — outcome (A), material directive required.

Plain finding: the claimed exact one-district simplex/LP frontier is not valid for the stated arbitrary-ADMG class. “One district” does not make the joint law of all response functions in that district an arbitrary simplex: missing bidirected edges still impose within-district latent-factor restrictions. In thm:one-district-fiber-projection the reverse construction introduces one U_D carrying the whole profile and lets every V∈D read it; for a non-bidirected-clique district this adds bidirected edges and is not compatible with the original latent-projection G. Minimal audit counterexample: three binary roots with G=A↔B↔C and no A↔C. Standard semi-Markovian compatibility uses independent U_AB,U_BC, so A and C response maps are independent; normalization-only K_D is the full simplex and contains a 50–50 law on (A,C)=(0,0),(1,1), which would require A↔C/common latent dependence. Thus {q_D(M)}≠K_D even though the visited variables form one district. All active-face iff, sharp dual-countermodel, sign-frontier, and acquisition claims that invoke this surjectivity inherit the problem.

“Repair and strengthen the paper around an explicit district-saturated response-block class. Add a model assumption saying that every district used by the exact local results is a bidirected clique generated by one unrestricted finite latent response block (equivalently, the graph semantics deliberately forgets internal bidirected sparsity and treats each district as one latent hyperedge). Under that assumption, replace the redundant one-hot-table/exogenous global parameterization by the direct source-labelled response-profile fiber
  q_D^s∈Δ(Ω_D),  q_D^s=q_D^⋆ for D∩Δ_s=∅,
  Ψ_{a,v}^s(q^s)=P_a^s(v) for every complete menu cell,
where Ψ_C^s(q^s)=Σ_{ω∈∏_DΩ_D}1{C(ω)}∏_D q_D^s(ω_D). Prove direct fixed-original-alphabet realization in both directions, state that every Ψ is multi-affine with degree at most the number of visited districts, and make the one-district collapse to a polytope/active-face LP the field-tier headline. Ensure A_D contains every raw complete-menu-cell incidence equality (or prove identity extraction always retains it), not merely successful derived extractions. For arbitrary nonsaturated ADMGs, retain the Zhang graph-compatible canonical polynomial fiber as the exact object and demote K_D to an outer relaxation; do not claim local iff/countermodels there. Replace ‘computable/exactly checkable’ by ‘finite semialgebraic characterization’ unless menu probabilities have an effective rational/algebraic encoding. Sync TL;DR, project_justification, related_work, interpretation, technical limitation, honest_scope, and every theorem consumer/gap. In particular, remove the current Gap sentence saying prior work does not lift a failed local face: this paper also does not lift it in the multi-district class.”

Why material/maximal: the saturated-class reframe both repairs the paper and yields a genuinely cheaper structured multi-affine global program (variables Σ_{s,D}(|Ω_D|−1), no one-hot structural-table variables), while preserving the exact active-face/arm-pruning headline. Staying with arbitrary ADMGs forces the one-district LP results down to sufficient outer-relaxation certificates.

CLASS AUDIT / LAUNDERING:
• Zhang–Tian–Bareinboim 2022 Thm 2.4 is for an arbitrary SCM but produces a canonical SCM with the SAME causal diagram and all joint counterfactual laws (PMLR PDF pp.3–4, Def.2.3/Thm2.4); this does not license replacing a sparse connected district by one shared unrestricted U_D. Thm2.8 (p.5, Eq.9) already gives sharp polynomial extrema from all supplied L1/L2 cell equalities.
• Correa–Lee–Bareinboim 2022 defines multi-domain selection-diagram models via vertex discrepancies (pp.3–5, Defs3.1–3.3); on a common-G district-closed subfamily, unchanged mechanisms/latent laws imply the note’s response-law invariance, so the note is a law-level relaxation/quotient of that published subclass, not literally the same published class. CTFTR’s input interventions include atomic, conditional, and stochastic policies (p.5), so ‘observational and hard-interventional’ understates its L2 scope. Thm5.1 (pp.8–9; Appendix B pp.19–20) is complete only for that Z,GΔ task. Its necessity proof explicitly enlarges an observed domain to X_A2×{0,1} (Appendix A, Lemma A.1, pp.11–12) and later appends path bits (pp.16–18), so it is not a fixed-original-alphabet converse.
• Raghavan–Bareinboim 2026 assumes finite discrete variables and positivity (§2, p.3), and Thm3.5 (p.6) is one SCM with input action set A; Appendix E.1 crucially uses physical realizability (Lem.E.6) and the CTFIDU+ converse makes each observable an (a′+1)-bit encoding (Lem.E.9, pp.29–30). Theorem C.2 (p.21) characterizes the realizable L2.5 class. Thus the note’s singleton-domain ‘embedding’ needs an actual grammar map covering every L2.5 action; the present assertion from ‘declared partial-copy’ syntax alone is not enough.
• The note’s global source-labelled canonical fiber is not itself a published named class. Its one-domain canonical slice is Zhang’s class, and Raghavan Appendix E.3 p.33 explicitly notes that added input regimes impose linear/polynomial constraints on canonical mapping parameters. The multi-domain product plus response-law equalities is a straightforward constrained product/reframe, so generic compactness+attained extrema should not be sold as the main novelty.
• No converse transfers upward: CTFTR failure with L1/L2 inputs can be repaired by added L3 inputs; CTFIDU+ failure in one SCM can be repaired by added source domains. Subclass nonidentification never proves superclass nonidentification here.

For each \(s\in\mathcal S\), let \(\theta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\) range over \(\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\), the finite canonical SCM parameterization obtained by enumerating the structural tables compatible with \(G\) and the declared observed alphabets.  Its coordinates obey
\[
 p_{U}^{s}(u)\geq 0,\qquad \sum_{u\in\Omega_U}p_U^s(u)=1,
 \qquad
 \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^{s}\in\{0,1\},\qquad
 \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^{s}=1.
\]
The canonical exogenous variables are assigned to their graph-compatible district blocks, and blocks belonging to distinct districts have product law.  Thus the displayed constraints include recursive compatibility with \(G\) and district factorization, while retaining the original alphabet \(\mathcal X_V\) at every observed vertex.

For any finite counterfactual event \(C\) in domain \(s\), recursively evaluate the one-hot tables in topological order and define the cell polynomial
\[
 \Phi_C^s(\theta^s)
 =\sum_{u\in\prod_U\Omega_U}
   \mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under }(\mu^s,u)\}
   \prod_U p_U^s(u_U).
\]
The indicator is itself a finite polynomial in the one-hot coordinates by recursive substitution.  For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), let \(q_D^s(\omega_D;\theta^s)\) be the analogous polynomial obtained by summing the same monomials over the canonical exogenous assignments whose induced structural response profile on \(D\) is \(\omega_D\).

\[
\begin{split}
 \Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta=(\theta^s:s\in\mathcal S):{}&
 \theta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
 &q_D^s(\cdot;\theta^s)=q_D^\star(\cdot;\theta^\star)
   \quad\text{whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
 &\Phi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v)
   \quad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s,
   \ v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
All graph, one-hot, simplex, district-factorization, invariance, and complete supplied-law constraints are retained.  For a target-domain counterfactual cell \(T\), set
\[
 L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_T^\star(\theta^\star),

 U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]

\[

Then \(\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}=\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). In particular, every point of the boundary face, not only its relative interior, is induced by a compatible SCM family on the declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\).
changed.to:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Suppose \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds. Then
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]

changed.reason: The current reverse inclusion is false for a sparse non-clique district: internal latent-factor restrictions can make the realizable district response set a strict subset of the full row face. The proposal retains the always-valid outer inclusion and restricts surjectivity to the explicit district-saturated, district-separated class.

changed.from: Suppose the union of variables visited by the reduced target and every retained menu factor has one district \(D\), and \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). A target row \(b_D\) is constant on \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) if and only if \[b_D\in\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}.\] If \(b_D=\lambda^\top A_D+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\), its value is \(\lambda^\top m_D\). If the membership fails, two SCM families on \(\mathcal X\) agree on every supplied law and disagree on the target cell.
changed.to:
For the broad compatibility fiber, the membership
\[
b_D\in\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\]
is sufficient for the district-local target \(b_Dq_D^\star\) to be identified, with value \(\lambda^\top m_D\) whenever
\[
b_D=\lambda^\top A_D+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\]
If additionally \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the membership is also necessary for constancy on \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\). On that saturated separated class, failure yields two compatible SCM families on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\) that agree on every supplied law and disagree on the target cell. changed.reason: Active-face membership is sufficient on the broad class, but necessity and paired-model realization require equality of the global district projection with the row face. The proposal states that equality only for the saturated separated subclass.

On either embedded class, every successful identifying functional returned by DCTFTR agrees semantically with the target query, and every successful functional returned by the published calculus agrees with that same query; no syntactic or transition-by-transition output equivalence is asserted. changed.from: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then \[\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.\] Consequently, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every compatible SCM if and only if the displayed dual has a certificate with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\), a primal minimizer induces an original-alphabet compatible SCM with \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)\), primal minimizers and maximizers induce two original-alphabet compatible SCMs with opposite arm rankings.
changed.to:
Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=
\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}
\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.
\]
Every feasible dual vector with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\) certifies \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every model in the broad fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If additionally \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, this certificate condition is also necessary for uniform strict dominance on the saturated fiber. Under these additional hypotheses, \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\) is attained by an original-alphabet compatible saturated SCM with \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\), and \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)\) yields two such SCM families with opposite strict rankings. Without the additional hypotheses, the primal optimizers need not lift from the row face.
changed.reason: LP duality and positive-certificate soundness hold on the row outer face, but the iff and countermodel conclusions require saturated separated surjectivity. The proposal separates these scopes.

changed.from: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces are obtained from the feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of one closed interval, allowing zero, one, or two sign boundaries; each boundary returns both a dual menu-weight certificate on the pruning side and an original-alphabet SCM attaining equality.
changed.to: Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces may be obtained from feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of a closed convex subset, which is empty, a point, or a closed interval, and has zero, one, or two relative sign boundaries. Each boundary has a dual menu-weight certificate of value zero and a primal row-face law attaining equality; the adjacent strict-pruning side has a positive dual piece. If the row-augmented supplied menu at that boundary has nonempty \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\) and satisfies \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), the equality law is realized by a district-saturated SCM on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\). Without those hypotheses, no SCM lifting of the row-face boundary is asserted.
changed.reason: The polyhedral value-function statement is unconditional, but an original-alphabet SCM at a boundary optimizer requires the corrected saturated separated projection theorem.

changed.from:
The minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are computable for every finite instance by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and solving the finite linear feasibility problems that define \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\).  In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular.  In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district instance with two unit-cost Layer-3 cell experiments for which
\[
 \operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
 =\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Consequently the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns.  For this instance the exact acquisition problem reduces to
\[
 \min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
 \quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
whose unique solution is \((x_1,x_2)=(1,1)\) with cost two.
The multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality is a matching dual lower-bound certificate for the continuous relaxation.
changed.to:
For every finite instance, all minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are characterized by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and, for each arm, solving the finite linear program consisting of the equations defining \(\mathcal K_S\), the common-denominator positivity test, and the pairwise numerator-gap inequalities. This is an algorithmic computation whenever all matrix entries, menu values, and costs are effectively presented rational or real algebraic numbers. In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular. In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district instance with two unit-cost Layer-3 cell experiments for which
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Consequently the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns. For this instance the exact acquisition problem is
\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
whose unique solution is \((x_1,x_2)=(1,1)\) with cost two. The multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality is a matching dual lower-bound certificate for the continuous relaxation.
changed.reason: Finite subset enumeration and LP feasibility characterize all solutions, but unconditional algorithmic computability is not meaningful for uneffectively specified real coefficients. The proposal claims an algorithm only for effectively presented rational or real-algebraic inputs and retains the finite characterization for arbitrary coefficients.

changed.from:
Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\).  The set \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set of finite dimension, and canonical realization on the declared observed alphabets gives, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
 \bigl\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):
       \mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
 =
 \bigl\{(\Phi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
       \theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\bigr\}.
\]
Consequently, the extrema \(L_T(\mathcal P)\) and \(U_T(\mathcal P)\) are attained and are the sharp bounds for every target cell \(T\).  The bounds are strictly tighter than the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when \(L_T(\mathcal P)>0\) or \(U_T(\mathcal P)<1\), an exactly checkable property of the displayed program.  The cell is identified if and only if \(L_T(\mathcal P)=U_T(\mathcal P)\); if \(L_T(\mathcal P)<U_T(\mathcal P)\), minimizing and maximizing canonical parameters yield two SCM families on the original observed alphabets that agree on every cell of every complete supplied law and disagree on \(T\).

Let
\[
 e_-=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star),
 \qquad
 e_+=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star).
\]
If \(e_+ =0\), the evidence has probability zero throughout the compatibility fiber; if \(e_-=0<e_+\), its positivity is not uniform.  In both cases a conditional functional on the entire fiber is rejected before division.  If \(e_->0\), the sharp range of the conditional arm value is
\[
 \left[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)},
 \quad
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)}
 \right],
\]
with both endpoints attained.  Under the same condition \(e_->0\), uniform strict ordering satisfies
\[
 \begin{array}{rcl}
 Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)>0,\\[3pt]
 Q_\rho^\star>Q_\sigma^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0,
 \end{array}
\]
and two original-alphabet compatible families with opposite strict rankings exist if and only if
\[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0
 <\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta).
\]
In particular, a target structural-causal bandit may safely prune \(\rho\) in favor of \(\sigma\) exactly when the first strict minimum condition holds.

For every district \(D\), the global projection satisfies
\[
 \{q_D^\star(\cdot;\theta^\star):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}
 \subseteq \mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
A local point, or a pair of local points, lifts to globally compatible SCM families exactly when it belongs, or they both belong, to the left-hand projection.  Equality with \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) follows under the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem, but is not implied in a multi-district problem.  Hence a local \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) face-failure trace alone is not a global paired-model certificate; the exact multi-district certificate is instead furnished by distinct optimizers of the displayed global polynomial programs.
changed.to:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
For a sparse nonsaturated graph or a cross-district-coupled menu, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is only an outer relaxation. Equality for the saturated fiber follows only under \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) by the one-district fiber-projection theorem. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside that theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.
changed.reason: One unrestricted district-response law is exact only for the saturated response-block class. The proposal gives that multi-affine frontier there and retains a separate graph-compatible canonical polynomial frontier for arbitrary sparse ADMGs. It states attained sharp extrema for declared target cells without claiming that disconnected scalar or conditional images fill the interval between them.

{"id":"thm:exact-global-canonical-frontier","kind":"theorem","statement":"There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
For a sparse nonsaturated graph or a cross-district-coupled menu, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is only an outer relaxation. Equality for the saturated fiber follows only under \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) by the one-district fiber-projection theorem. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside that theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.","free_symbols":["\Theta(\mathcal P)","\mathcal P","\mathcal C(\mathcal P)","\mathcal F","C","\mathbf M","\mathcal X","\Phi_C^s(\theta)","\theta","\star","T","L_T(\mathcal P)","U_T(\mathcal P)","E","e_-","e_+","B_\rho","\rho","\sigma","Q_\rho^\star","\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)","D","q_D^s","\mathcal K_D(m_D)","m_D","\mathsf{DCTFTR}"],"depends_on":["ass:recursive-compatibility","ass:district-factorization","ass:district-kernel-invariance","ass:district-closure","ass:typed-menu-realizability","def:model-class","def:compatibility-fiber","def:exact-global-canonical-fiber","lem:finite-canonical-counterfactual-equivalence","lem:district-cell-linearity","thm:one-district-fiber-projection"],"status":"to-prove","justification":"The exact multi-district object is the global canonical compatibility fiber, not the Cartesian product of locally extracted district faces.","gap":"Complete source-menu cells impose cross-district polynomial equalities that a local face omits; canonical finite-SCM reduction retains those equalities while preserving the declared observed alphabets.","consumer":"Target-cell bounds, conditional Layer-3 identification, and Park--Lee-style arm pruning can use attained global optimizers as auditable same-menu certificates."}

There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
For a sparse nonsaturated graph or a cross-district-coupled menu, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is only an outer relaxation. Equality for the saturated fiber follows only under \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) by the one-district fiber-projection theorem. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside that theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.

{"id":"thm:exact-global-canonical-frontier","kind":"theorem","statement":"There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
For a sparse nonsaturated graph or a cross-district-coupled menu, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is only an outer relaxation. If \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
which requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of all \(D'\ne D\). This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation is what makes the displayed multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.","free_symbols":["\mathcal C(\mathcal P)","\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)","\mathcal P","\Theta(\mathcal P)","\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)","\mathcal F","C","\mathbf M","\mathcal X","\Psi_C^s(\theta)","\theta","\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta)","\vartheta","\star","T","E","B_\rho","\rho","\sigma","Q_\rho^\star","D","\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)","\mathcal K_D(m_D)","m_D","\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)"],"depends_on":["ass:recursive-compatibility","ass:district-factorization","ass:district-kernel-invariance","ass:district-closure","ass:typed-menu-realizability","def:model-class","def:district-saturated-model-class","def:compatibility-fiber","def:saturated-compatibility-fiber","def:exact-global-canonical-fiber","def:compatible-face","def:district-separated-menu","lem:finite-canonical-counterfactual-equivalence","lem:district-cell-linearity","thm:one-district-fiber-projection"],"status":"to-prove","justification":"The exact multi-district object is the global canonical compatibility fiber, not the Cartesian product of locally extracted district faces.","gap":"Complete source-menu cells impose cross-district polynomial equalities that a local face omits; canonical finite-SCM reduction retains those equalities while preserving the declared observed alphabets.","consumer":"Target-cell bounds, conditional Layer-3 identification, and Park--Lee-style arm pruning can use attained global optimizers as auditable same-menu certificates."}

changed.from:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]

There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

\[

\]

\[

\[

\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}
\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.
\]
Every feasible dual vector with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\) certifies \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every model in the broad fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If additionally \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, this certificate condition is also necessary for uniform strict dominance on the focal-district-saturated fiber. changed.from: Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces may be obtained from feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of a closed convex subset, which is empty, a point, or a closed interval, and has zero, one, or two relative sign boundaries. Each boundary has a dual menu-weight certificate of value zero and a primal row-face law attaining equality; the adjacent strict-pruning side has a positive dual piece. If the supplied menu augmented by the boundary equality \(r_D^\dagger q=p\) has a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber and satisfies its \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\) predicate, the equality law is realized by an SCM saturated only at \(D\) on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\), with every district \(D'\ne D\) retaining its original graph-compatible restrictions. The structural predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\) is a sufficient check for this active-slice condition. Without those hypotheses, no SCM lifting of the row-face boundary is asserted.

changed.from:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
If \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
which requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of all \(D'\ne D\). Cross-district coupling of a complete supplied cell does not by itself defeat this equality: it is harmless whenever each fixed-nonfocal focal slice lies in \(R_D(m_D)\). The older structural predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) is sufficient but not necessary for this active-slice condition. Outside focal-district saturation and active-slice separation, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is certified only as an outer relaxation. This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation is what makes the displayed multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.

{"id":"thm:exact-global-canonical-frontier","kind":"theorem","statement":"There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
If \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
and \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) itself entails a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber. This equality requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of every \(D'\ne D\). Cross-district coupling of a complete supplied cell is harmless for the fixed-baseline replacement exactly when its baseline-averaged focal row lies in \(R_D(m_D)\), because
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a baseline-free sufficient certificate for this equality. The baseline-averaged predicate is generally baseline-dependent and not directly checkable from menu cells alone; allowing a different baseline for each candidate \(q\) is not asserted. Outside focal-district saturation and baseline-averaged separation, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is certified only as an outer relaxation. This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation makes the multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.","free_symbols":["\mathcal C(\mathcal P)","\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)","\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)","\mathcal P","\Theta(\mathcal P)","\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)","\mathcal F","C","\mathbf M","\mathcal X","\Psi_C^s(\theta)","\theta","\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta)","\vartheta","\star","T","E","B_\rho","\rho","\sigma","Q_\rho^\star","D","\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)","\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)","\mathcal K_D(m_D)","m_D","R_D(m_D)","\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)","\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)"],"depends_on":["ass:recursive-compatibility","ass:district-factorization","ass:district-kernel-invariance","ass:district-closure","ass:typed-menu-realizability","def:model-class","def:district-saturated-model-class","def:focal-district-saturated-model-class","def:compatibility-fiber","def:saturated-compatibility-fiber","def:exact-global-canonical-fiber","def:compatible-face","def:district-separated-menu","def:active-slice-separated-menu","lem:structural-separation-implies-active-slice","lem:finite-canonical-counterfactual-equivalence","lem:district-cell-linearity","thm:one-district-fiber-projection"],"status":"to-prove","justification":"The theorem separates exact all-district multi-affine variation, exact sparse canonical optimization, and exact active-slice focal-district geometry.","gap":"Global programs retain every cross-district polynomial equality; locally, such coupling is also preserved when every fixed-nonfocal focal indicator slice belongs to the active row space.","consumer":"Global target bounds and arm pruning use attained exact-program optimizers, while local LP certificates use focal saturation plus the weaker active-slice condition."}

\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
The baseline-averaged active-slice predicate \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when there exists one \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
