changed.reason: Use the complete query-independent response carrier so later targets and acquired regimes cannot visit omitted parent configurations.

changed.from: For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal X_{W_a})\), write \[\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\] exactly when consistency, unnesting, ancestor restriction, fixing, and marginalization define a kernel \(K_{s,a,D}:H_{s,a,D}\to\Delta(C_{s,a,D})\) and \(\kappa\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) certifies every context, marginal, and nonzero divisor used. An undefined fixing, unavailable context, or uncertified quotient has no successful judgment.
changed.to:
For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal Y_a)\), write
\[
\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)
\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)
\]
exactly when the finite extraction calculus constructs, for every retained \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), a numerator event \(A_{h,c}\), a context event \(H_h\), derivations
\[
\delta_N:A_{h,c}\Downarrow N_{s,a,D,h,c},
\qquad
\delta_H:H_h\Downarrow H_{s,a,D,h},
\]
two accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) traces, the rows those traces construct,
\[
r_{s,a,D,h,c}=\operatorname{row}_D(A_{h,c}),
\qquad
v_{s,a,D,h}=\operatorname{row}_D(H_h),
\]
and an independently checkable certificate \(\pi_h\) that \(H_{s,a,D,h}>0\) on the declared fiber.  The returned kernel entry is the typed expression
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=
\operatorname{Quot}(N_{s,a,D,h,c},H_{s,a,D,h},\pi_h).
\]
The record \(\kappa\) contains only the event and expression derivations, locality tables, constructed rows, and positivity certificates.  It contains neither \(N=r^{\mathsf T}q\), nor \(H=v^{\mathsf T}q\), nor any equivalent semantic equality.  An unavailable cell, undefined fixing, rejected locality table, or uncertified denominator has no successful judgment and creates no row-eligibility record.
changed.reason: Separate constructive numerator and context derivations, exhaustive locality traces, and positivity certificates from the row equalities later proved.

changed.from: \[r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{\omega_D\text{ produces extracted cell }c\text{ at context }h\text{ under regime }a\},\qquad\omega_D\in\Omega_D.\]
changed.to:
For every successful row-eligibility record define the separate numerator and context rows
\[
\begin{split}
r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)
&=\mathbf 1\{A_{h,c}\text{ has the common value certified by }
\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\},\\
v_{s,a,D,h}(\omega_D)
&=\mathbf 1\{H_h\text{ has the common value certified by }
\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\},
\end{split}
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
For a complete supplied output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\), an accepting locality trace similarly constructs
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}=\operatorname{row}_D(C_{a,y}).
\]
The quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) is not an incidence row.
changed.reason: Construct numerator, context, and raw output-cell rows separately and never treat a conditional quotient as an incidence row.

changed.from:
For each complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  If recursive evaluation of \(C_{a,v}\) visits only \(D\), retain before all derived rows the raw identity-extraction row
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under }\omega_D\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D,
\]
with value \(P_a^s(v)\).  Thus every transport-admissible complete-menu cell whose reduction is district-local is retained even when no nontrivial fixing quotient is available.  Next, for every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) with the same admissibility proof, retain every available row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\).  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^\top\), stack the normalization row, raw rows, and derived rows in canonical order as \(A_D\), and stack their values as \(m_D\).  A failed derived extraction creates no derived row, but it does not delete an independently certified raw district-local row.  A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.
changed.to:
Fix \(D\).  Enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete output cell, and extraction record canonically.  A candidate is transport admissible only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  First retain every admissible complete output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) whose exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) table accepts, with row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}\) and supplied value \(P_a^s(y)\).  Next, for every successful extraction judgment retain separately the numerator pair
\[
(r_{s,a,D,h,c},N_{s,a,D,h,c})
\]
and the context pair
\[
(v_{s,a,D,h},H_{s,a,D,h}).
\]
Never stack the quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) as a linear row.  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one and stack precisely the accepted raw, numerator, and context rows as \(A_D\), with their values in the same order as \(m_D\).  A failed locality, fixing, expression, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.  A rejected complete cell remains, without information loss, among the complete polynomial equalities of the exact global fiber.  For a deterministic postprocessor, recursive locality and the raw incidence row use the preimage identity \((1)\) from \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), but the stacked value is the directly supplied output probability \(P_a^s(y)\).
changed.reason: Stack only proved raw, numerator, and context equalities, while preserving every rejected cross-district cell in the exact global fiber.

changed.from: Reduce \(B_\rho\cap E\) and \(E\) to target-district cells and evaluate them on \(\Omega_D\), obtaining \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(d_D\); set \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\). The same reduction applied to any target cell gives \(b_D\).
changed.to:
For a fixed district \(D\), a total record \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) consists of: a finite nonempty arm set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); for every \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(B_\rho\cap E)\) trace and its constructed row \(n_{\rho,D}\); one accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(E)\) trace and its constructed row \(d_D\); a rational or real-algebraic number \(\varepsilon_D>0\); and an exact certificate that
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D
\qquad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Only from such a record define, for \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\),
\[
Q_\rho(q)=\frac{n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q},
\qquad
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}.
\]
Separately, for any target cell \(C\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) trace constructs the generic target row \(b_D=\operatorname{row}_D(C)\).  If a required locality trace rejects, the corresponding row, comparison, or target value is undefined rather than silently assigned a row.
changed.reason: Require a total locality record and a uniform positive common-evidence certificate before any conditional arm comparison is defined.

changed.from: \[\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\min_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q,\qquad \overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\max_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q.\]
changed.to:
Given a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record and \(\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), define
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
=\min_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q,
\qquad
\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
=\max_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q.
\]
The definitions are made only when the checked record exists; its positivity certificate makes every associated conditional comparison well defined on the face.
changed.reason: Make the margin depend on the total checked-local-arms record.

changed.from: A certificate at level \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) satisfying \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) coordinatewise and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\ge\gamma\).
changed.to:
Given a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record, \(\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), a menu-dual dominance certificate at level \(\gamma\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}\) satisfying
\[
A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}
\leq g_{\rho,\sigma,D}
\quad\text{coordinatewise},
\qquad
m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\geq\gamma.
\]
It is not defined in the absence of the total locality and common-evidence record.
changed.reason: Type the dual certificate only after all arm rows and their common positive evidence row are checked.

changed.from: \[I_D=\{r_D^\dagger q:q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\},\qquad\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=\min_{\substack{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\\ r_D^\dagger q=p}}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q,\qquad\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=\{p\in I_D:\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)>0\}.\]
changed.to:
Given a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record and a realizable additional complete Layer-3 output-cell row \(r_D^\dagger\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\), define
\[
I_D=\{(r_D^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}q:q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
For \(p\in I_D\), define
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)
=\min_{\substack{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\\
(r_D^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}q=p}}
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q,
\qquad
\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+
=\{p\in I_D:\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)>0\}.
\]
Every object is defined only from the checked arm rows and their common strictly positive evidence row.
changed.reason: Define the frontier only from a complete realizable output-cell row and the total checked arm system.

changed.from: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]
changed.to:
Fix a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record.  Each \(e\in\mathcal U\) is a realizable finite block of typed descriptors, possibly with deterministic finite postprocessing.  Acquiring \(e\) reveals the complete finite law of every declared output, including every normalization-dependent complementary cell, equivalently a dependent row-value block \((R_e,p_e)\), at cost \(c_e>0\).  Require joint realizability of the whole experiment menu:
\[
\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal U\}
\ne\varnothing.
\]
For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define
\[
\mathcal K_S
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\}.
\]
The checked lower bound \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D>0\) persists on every subface.  Hence define the possibly optimal set without a redundant evidence constraint by
\[
\operatorname{PO}(S)
=\left\{\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}:
\exists q\in\mathcal K_S\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ 
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})^{\mathsf T}q\geq0\right\}.
\]
Finally set
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),
\qquad
f(S)=|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|-|\operatorname{PO}(S)|,
\]
and define the exact ex-post acquisition problem by
\[
\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}.
\]
changed.reason: Require complete output-law blocks, joint realizability, and the total checked arm system.

changed.from: Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so the invariant district is \(D=\{Y\}\). Set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\), \(B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_0\ne Y_1\}\), \(B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_1=1\}\), and \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\). Order \(\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set \[A_D=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^\top,\quad \mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\le p\le1/2\},\quad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.\] The event incidence rows are \(n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0)\), \(n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1)\), and \(d_D=(1,1,1,1)\), so \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1)\). The sole block has \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), \(R_{e^\dagger}=r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1)\), and reveals the genuine Layer-3 source cell \(p_{e^\dagger}=p=P^s(Y_0=1,Y_1=1)=3/8\). Also set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).
changed.to:
Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so \(D=\{Y\}\) is invariant.  Order
\[
\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}
\]
for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set
\[
A_D=\begin{bmatrix}
1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=
\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\leq p\leq1/2\},
\qquad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.
\]
Take \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\),
\[
B_\rho=\{Y_0\ne Y_1\},
\qquad B_\sigma=\{Y_1=1\}.
\]
The exhaustive locality tables construct
\[
n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0),\quad
n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1),\quad
d_D=(1,1,1,1),
\]
and \(\varepsilon_D=1\) with the exact identity \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q=1\) on the face; these data form \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\).  Hence
\[
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1).
\]
Let \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\), \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), and let \(e^\dagger\) return the Boolean output
\[
f^\dagger(Y_0,Y_1)=\mathbf 1\{(Y_0,Y_1)=(1,1)\}.
\]
The complete source output law has \(P_{e^\dagger}^s(1)=3/8\) and \(P_{e^\dagger}^s(0)=5/8\).  Its output-one row is
\[
r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1),
\]
the output-zero row is its normalization-dependent complement, and \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}=\{q(3/8)\}\ne\varnothing\).  Finally set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).
changed.reason: Make the acquired Layer-3 object a legal complete Boolean output law and display its complement and joint realizability.

changed.from: \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) is the typed expression-and-certificate algebra generated from menu cells by finite sums, differences, products, marginalization sums, and quotients carrying a proof that the divisor is nonzero on the relevant compatibility fiber.
changed.to: The algebra \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) is generated by rational constants and the directly supplied complete output-cell probabilities \(P_a^s(y)\), including deterministic-pushforward output cells, under finite sums, differences, products, and marginalization sums.  It contains a quotient \(F/H\) only together with an independently checked certificate that \(H\ne0\) on the relevant compatibility fiber; a conditional causal output requires the stronger stored certificate \(H>0\) throughout that fiber.  A quantifier-free semialgebraic range or endpoint description returned by the canonical quantifier-elimination fallback is represented by \(\mathsf{HybridResult}\), not declared to belong to \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\).
changed.reason: Distinguish rational fast-path functionals from quantifier-free canonical range descriptions.

changed.from:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, regimes, districts, assignments, and generated DAG-node identifiers. The event grammar is \[\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]\,V_{\alpha}=v,\qquad \mathsf{Event}::=	op\mid ot\mid\mathsf{Atom}\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},\] where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term and canonical normalized events are disjoint normal forms of unnested atoms. Identified expressions have grammar \[\mathsf{Expr}::=\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,u)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,G,
u_G),\] where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(
u_G\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate. The phase-indexed node grammar is exactly \[\mathsf{Goal}::=\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\mid\operatorname{Normed}(	au,e,
u)\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e,\alpha)\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),\] with \(	au\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\). A configuration is a finite well-typed acyclic work DAG of these nodes, its numerator and denominator roots, and a checked trace. For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), node denotation is defined recursively: the first three event phases denote their target event probability; \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\) and \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\) denote \(bq_D^\star(\mathbf M)\); \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta)\) denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\); and sum and product nodes denote the corresponding finite sum and product of child denotations. Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root values. Checked derivations are finite syntax trees: normalization derivations use only consistency, unnesting, contradiction, Boolean normalization, and finite disjoint-additivity constructors; ancestor derivations enumerate summed assignments; district-split derivations enumerate the districts of \(G[H]\) and use finite marginalization and semi-Markovian district factorization; extraction derivations record each fixing, marginalization, context lookup, and certified quotient; face certificates are exact rational LP or Farkas certificates; and zero, nonzero, or strict-positivity certificates are checked by exact rational ring normalization together with Farkas certificates for linear face constraints or displayed sum-of-squares preordering identities for the finite response-law constraints. Thus no certificate constructor consists merely of the semantic equality or inequality being certified. The terminals are \[\mathsf{Result}::=\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t),\] where a conditioning derivation \(\delta\) records the numerator derivation, denominator derivation, and positivity certificate. Failure constructors include \(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t)\), \(\operatorname{EXTRACTION\_UNDEFINED}(s,a,D,h)\), \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t)\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}(D,b,\mathrm{retainedRows},t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t)\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t)\).
changed.to:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, domains, descriptors, districts, assignments, complete response profiles, and generated work-DAG identifiers.  The counterfactual syntax is
\[
\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]V_\alpha=v,
\qquad
\mathsf{Event}::=\top\mid\bot\mid\mathsf{Atom}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},
\]
where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term.  A descriptor declares a finite returned counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\).  Its output cell is the event \(\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\); the parser uses the pointwise preimage identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}
\tag{1}
\]
only for normalization, locality tables, and response-profile evaluation.  The expression leaf for this cell is the directly supplied number \(P_a^s(y)\), not a collection of unsupplied tuple-cell probabilities.  Normalized events are canonical disjoint normal forms of consistent unnested atoms, including contradiction and sure-event forms.

Identified expressions have grammar
\[
\mathsf{Expr}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\nu_H),
\]
where \(J\) is finite, \(r\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\nu_H\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate on the declared fiber.  The phase-indexed work-node grammar is
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{Goal}::={}&
\operatorname{Raw}(\tau,e)
\mid\operatorname{Normed}(\tau,e,\nu)
\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(\tau,H,e,\alpha)
\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\\
&\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(\tau,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)
\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),
\end{split}
\]
with \(\tau\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\) and an accepting locality trace \(\ell\) on every row-needed node.  A configuration \(\mathsf{Config}\) is a finite well-typed acyclic DAG of these nodes, two distinguished roots, and a checked transition trace.

For \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), raw, normalized, and ancestor-closed nodes denote their target-domain event probabilities.  A row or face node at \((D,b)\) denotes \(b^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\), a resolved node denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\), and sum and product nodes denote the finite sum and product of their children.  Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root denotations.  Normalization derivations check consistency, unnesting, \((1)\), and finite disjoint Boolean identities pointwise.  Ancestor derivations enumerate every marginalized assignment.  Split derivations expand over the original districts \(\mathcal D(G)\), never over districts newly formed in an induced subgraph.  Extraction derivations are finite \(\mathsf{XEvent}\)- and \(\mathsf{XExpr}\)-trees with exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) tables, separate numerator and context rows, and independent positivity certificates; they contain no semantic row equality.  A face node is well typed only after literal verification of every equation in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\).  Its row-space and forced-zero certificates use exact rational or real-algebraic linear arithmetic.  Zero, nonzero, and strict-positivity certificates are independently checked rational identities, exact linear certificates, or displayed finite preordering identities; none may consist of the conclusion it certifies.

The terminals are
\[
\mathsf{Result}::=
\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)
\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t).
\]
Failure traces include ill-typed normalization or deterministic-preimage parsing, undefined original-district splitting, failed locality or extraction, \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).  For a nonterminal configuration define
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}
=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi,r_C)\in\mathbb N^8,
\]
counting respectively raw, normalized, ancestor-closed, row-needed, face-needed, unresolved-sum, unresolved-product nodes, and one terminalization flag; every terminal has rank zero.
changed.reason: Add deterministic postprocessing, constructive extraction trees, exhaustive locality traces, and original-district typing.

changed.from:
Initialize one finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_ho\wedge E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\); its denotation at \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) is \((P_{M^\star}(B_ho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\). The deterministic transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has these eight rules. \(\mathsf{NORM}\): replace the least \(\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\) by \(\operatorname{Normed}(	au,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\), where the total finite-state checker applies consistency, unnesting, contradiction removal, and disjoint-normal-form rewriting and returns a derivation \(
u:P(e)=P(\operatorname{nf}(e))\); append \(\operatorname{NORM}(v,e,\operatorname{nf}(e),

changed.to:
Initialize a finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_\rho\cap E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\).  The deterministic priority rules are \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\), and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\), using the rank from \(\mathrm{def:dctftr\text{-}grammar}\) and least-node tie breaking.

The normalization rule expands deterministic output cells only through the pointwise preimage identity and checks Boolean equality.  The ancestor rule records its complete finite marginalization identity.  At split, run \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) for every original district in canonical order.  An accepting trace creates \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\).  If no original district is local, splice the exact original-district expansion
\[
P_{M^\star}(C)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1_C(\omega)
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^\star(\omega_D)
\tag{1}
\]
as a finite sum-product DAG.  No factorization over districts newly formed by an induced subgraph is used.  An enumeration or typing failure returns its typed split failure.

At extraction, enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete supplied output cell, and constructive extraction record.  Retain a candidate only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  Retain a raw output-cell row only when its exhaustive locality table accepts, and retain every derived numerator and context row separately.  Never retain a conditional quotient as a row.  Prepend normalization, construct \((A_D,m_D)\) exactly as in \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\), and replay the derivations to check each equality in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\) literally.  Rejected candidates are recorded and remain constraints of the global canonical fiber.

At face identification, compute the forced-zero set by exact linear programming and accept only a checked representation
\[
b_D=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_D+
\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\tag{2}
\]
It then resolves the node to \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}m_D\).  Failure of membership returns \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), whose witness concerns only the local row relaxation; when only normalization survives, the same failed face test is labelled \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\).  Ready sum and product rules use finite additivity and the original-district factorization in \((1)\).

Condition returns uniform zero evidence only with an independent certificate, divides only with an independent certificate of strict positivity throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), returns a displayed compatible zero-evidence model when available, and otherwise returns uncertified positivity.  In priority order, the first seven rules decrease respectively \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi\), fix every earlier coordinate, and create no earlier-phase node; condition decreases \(r_C\) only after the other coordinates vanish.  Every partial operation has its stated failure branch, so \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.

\[

\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad

\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]

\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,

{"id":"def:finite-extraction-calculus","name":"Finite constructive extraction calculus","construction":"The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.","free_symbols":["\mathsf{XEvent}","\mathsf{XExpr}","\mathsf{FixTrace}","s","a","T_a","f_a","\mathcal Y_a","P_a^s","\mathcal P","\mathscr R(\mathcal P)","D","\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D","\operatorname{row}_D","\Omega_D","\mathcal K_D(m_D)"],"inputs":["G","\mathcal X","\mathcal P"]}

{"id":"def:dctftr-grammar","name":"DCTFTR syntax, configurations, and terminals","construction":"Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, domains, descriptors, districts, assignments, complete response profiles, and generated work-DAG identifiers.  The counterfactual syntax is
\[
\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]V_\alpha=v,
\qquad
\mathsf{Event}::=\top\mid\bot\mid\mathsf{Atom}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},
\]
where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term.  A descriptor declares a finite returned counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\).  Its output cell is the event \(\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\); the parser uses the pointwise preimage identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}
\tag{1}
\]
only for normalization, locality tables, and response-profile evaluation.  The expression leaf for this cell is the directly supplied number \(P_a^s(y)\), not a collection of unsupplied tuple-cell probabilities.  Normalized events are canonical disjoint normal forms of consistent unnested atoms, including contradiction and sure-event forms.

Identified expressions have grammar
\[
\mathsf{Expr}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\nu_H),
\]
where \(J\) is finite, \(r\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\nu_H\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate on the declared fiber.  The phase-indexed work-node grammar is
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{Goal}::={}&
\operatorname{Raw}(\tau,e)
\mid\operatorname{Normed}(\tau,e,\nu)
\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(\tau,H,e,\alpha)
\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\\
&\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(\tau,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)
\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),
\end{split}
\]
with \(\tau\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\) and an accepting locality trace \(\ell\) on every row-needed node.  A configuration \(\mathsf{Config}\) is a finite well-typed acyclic DAG of these nodes, two distinguished roots, and a checked transition trace.

For \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), raw, normalized, and ancestor-closed nodes denote their target-domain event probabilities.  A row or face node at \((D,b)\) denotes \(b^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\), a resolved node denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\), and sum and product nodes denote the finite sum and product of their children.  Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root denotations.  Normalization derivations check consistency, unnesting, \((1)\), and finite disjoint Boolean identities pointwise.  Ancestor derivations enumerate every marginalized assignment.  Split derivations expand over the original districts \(\mathcal D(G)\), never over districts newly formed in an induced subgraph.  Extraction derivations are finite \(\mathsf{XEvent}\)- and \(\mathsf{XExpr}\)-trees with exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) tables, separate numerator and context rows, and independent positivity certificates; they contain no semantic row equality.  A face node is well typed only after literal verification of every equation in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\).  Its row-space and forced-zero certificates use exact rational or real-algebraic linear arithmetic.  Zero, nonzero, and strict-positivity certificates are independently checked rational identities, exact linear certificates, or displayed finite preordering identities; none may consist of the conclusion it certifies.

The terminals are
\[
\mathsf{Result}::=
\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)
\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t).
\]
Failure traces include ill-typed normalization or deterministic-preimage parsing, undefined original-district splitting, failed locality or extraction, \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).  For a nonterminal configuration define
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}
=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi,r_C)\in\mathbb N^8,
\]
counting respectively raw, normalized, ancestor-closed, row-needed, face-needed, unresolved-sum, unresolved-product nodes, and one terminalization flag; every terminal has rank zero.","free_symbols":["\mathsf{Atom}","\mathsf{Event}","\mathsf{Goal}","\mathsf{Expr}","\mathsf{Config}","\mathsf{Result}","F_E","s","a","D","h","E","G","\mathbf M","\mathcal C(\mathcal P)","\mathcal P","q_D^s","\star","\mathscr R(\mathcal P)"],"inputs":["G","\mathcal X","\mathcal P"]}

{"id":"def:hybrid-result-grammar","name":"Real-semantic quantifier-elimination hybrid terminal grammar","construction":"Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring generated by the finitely many supplied rational or real-algebraic output-cell probabilities.  Their stipulated effective presentations give exact arithmetic and sign comparison in \(\mathbb D\), and an order-preserving embedding \(\mathbb D\hookrightarrow\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) supplies exact coefficient representations.  A \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) is finite syntax for a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign tests with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\).  For every real-closed field \(K\) containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\), this syntax has the usual realization \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_K\) in its displayed free variables.  In particular, the causal realization used below is \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_{\mathbb R}\) over the ordinary real field; neither canonical probability variables nor free target-value variables are restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

The hybrid terminal grammar is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{HybridResult}::={}&
\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}(\chi_T,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton})\\
&\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}
\mid\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\\
&\mid\operatorname{COND\_QE}(\chi_Q,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton}),
\end{split}
\tag{1}
\]
where each displayed \(\chi\) is a \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) and \(\mathsf{isSingleton}\) is the exact Boolean output of the associated closed first-order sentence.

The deterministic procedure \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) first runs \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).  A successful rational identification is returned as \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}\).  Every other terminal invokes the graph-compatible canonical fiber
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P).
\]
Every quantifier-elimination call below is made in the first-order language of real-closed fields with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\); its computation performs only exact coefficient operations in \(\mathbb D\), and its returned syntax is interpreted over \(\mathbb R\).  For \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\), apply quantifier elimination to
\[
\varphi_T(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{2}
\]
and denote the output by \(\chi_T(t)\).  Apply it to the closed sentence
\[
\exists t_1,t_2\,[\chi_T(t_1)\wedge\chi_T(t_2)\wedge t_1\ne t_2]
\tag{3}
\]
and to
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t],
\qquad
\chi_T(u)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow t\leq u]
\tag{4}
\]
to form the singleton Boolean and endpoint formulas.

For a conditional target put \(e=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\) and \(n=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf N:&\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0]
\ \wedge\ \exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0].
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Three quantifier-elimination calls yield closed quantifier-free formulas whose exact constant sign evaluations decide \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\).  The first two return the corresponding payload-free evidence terminals.  Only in case \(\mathsf P\) is quantifier elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_Q(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{6}
\]
to form \(\chi_Q(t)\), its singleton Boolean, and endpoint formulas as in \((3)\)--\((4)\).  The procedure returns formulas and decisions only: it returns no explicit endpoint value, algebraic sample, cylindrical algebraic decomposition trace, canonical parameter, or paired SCM.","free_symbols":["\mathsf{QEFormula}","\mathsf{HybridResult}","\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}","\mathsf{DCTFTR}","\mathscr R(\mathcal P)","\mathcal P","\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)","T","\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta)","E","B_\rho","\rho"],"inputs":["\mathcal P","\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)","\mathsf{DCTFTR}"]}

Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring generated by the finitely many supplied rational or real-algebraic output-cell probabilities.  Their stipulated effective presentations give exact arithmetic and sign comparison in \(\mathbb D\), and an order-preserving embedding \(\mathbb D\hookrightarrow\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) supplies exact coefficient representations.  A \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) is finite syntax for a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign tests with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\).  For every real-closed field \(K\) containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\), this syntax has the usual realization \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_K\) in its displayed free variables.  In particular, the causal realization used below is \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_{\mathbb R}\) over the ordinary real field; neither canonical probability variables nor free target-value variables are restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

The hybrid terminal grammar is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{HybridResult}::={}&
\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}(\chi_T,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton})\\
&\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}
\mid\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\\
&\mid\operatorname{COND\_QE}(\chi_Q,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton}),
\end{split}
\tag{1}
\]
where each displayed \(\chi\) is a \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) and \(\mathsf{isSingleton}\) is the exact Boolean output of the associated closed first-order sentence.

The deterministic procedure \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) first runs \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).  A successful rational identification is returned as \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}\).  Every other terminal invokes the graph-compatible canonical fiber
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P).
\]
Every quantifier-elimination call below is made in the first-order language of real-closed fields with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\); its computation performs only exact coefficient operations in \(\mathbb D\), and its returned syntax is interpreted over \(\mathbb R\).  For \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\), apply quantifier elimination to
\[
\varphi_T(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{2}
\]
and denote the output by \(\chi_T(t)\).  Apply it to the closed sentence
\[
\exists t_1,t_2\,[\chi_T(t_1)\wedge\chi_T(t_2)\wedge t_1\ne t_2]
\tag{3}
\]
and to
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t],
\qquad
\chi_T(u)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow t\leq u]
\tag{4}
\]
to form the singleton Boolean and endpoint formulas.

For a conditional target put \(e=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\) and \(n=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf N:&\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0]
\ \wedge\ \exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0].
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Three quantifier-elimination calls yield closed quantifier-free formulas whose exact constant sign evaluations decide \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\).  The first two return the corresponding payload-free evidence terminals.  Only in case \(\mathsf P\) is quantifier elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_Q(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{6}
\]
to form \(\chi_Q(t)\), its singleton Boolean, and endpoint formulas as in \((3)\)--\((4)\).  The procedure returns formulas and decisions only: it returns no explicit endpoint value, algebraic sample, cylindrical algebraic decomposition trace, canonical parameter, or paired SCM.

{"id":"def:hybrid-result-grammar","name":"Real-semantic quantifier-elimination hybrid terminal grammar","construction":"Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring generated by the finitely many supplied rational or real-algebraic output-cell probabilities.  Their stipulated effective presentations give exact arithmetic and sign comparison in \(\mathbb D\), and an order-preserving embedding \(\mathbb D\hookrightarrow\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) supplies exact coefficient representations.  A \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) is finite syntax for a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign tests with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\).  For every real-closed field \(K\) containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\), this syntax has the usual realization \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_K\) in its displayed free variables.  In particular, the causal realization used below is \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_{\mathbb R}\) over the ordinary real field; neither canonical probability variables nor free target-value variables are restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

The hybrid terminal grammar is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{HybridResult}::={}&
\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}(\chi_T,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton})\\
&\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}
\mid\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\\
&\mid\operatorname{COND\_QE}(\chi_Q,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton}),
\end{split}
\tag{1}
\]
where each displayed \(\chi\) is a \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) and \(\mathsf{isSingleton}\) is the exact Boolean output of the associated closed first-order sentence.

The deterministic procedure \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) first runs \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).  A successful rational identification is returned as \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}\).  Every other terminal invokes the graph-compatible canonical fiber
\[

\[

In the remaining case \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\) holds and the acquisition problem is defined, even if \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\varnothing)\) fails.

For every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) is decided exactly by one closed quantifier-elimination call.  Whenever it holds, there exists \(\epsilon_S>0\) such that
\[
\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star)\geq\epsilon_S
\qquad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\Lambda_S,
\]
and, for each \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), membership \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is decided exactly by one closed existential formula over the reals.  Moreover,
\[
S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bigl(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{Pos}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})\bigr),
\]
and, when both possibly-optimal sets are defined,
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(T_{\mathrm{exp}})
\subseteq\operatorname{PO}_G(S).
\]
Consequently the feasible design family is upward closed.  Exhaustive enumeration returns every minimum-cost solution, including every cost tie, using at most
\[
2^{|\mathcal U|}
\]
subset-positivity quantifier-elimination calls and at most
\[
2^{|\mathcal U|}|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|
\]
membership calls, in addition to one joint-realizability call and a fixed full-fiber status classification.

\[

Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring generated by the finitely many supplied rational or real-algebraic output-cell probabilities.  Their stipulated effective presentations give exact arithmetic and sign comparison in \(\mathbb D\), and an order-preserving embedding \(\mathbb D\hookrightarrow\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) supplies exact coefficient representations.  A \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) is finite syntax for a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign tests with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\).  For every real-closed field \(K\) containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\), this syntax has the usual realization \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_K\) in its displayed free variables.  In particular, the causal realization used below is \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_{\mathbb R}\) over the ordinary real field; neither canonical probability variables nor free target-value variables are restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

The hybrid terminal grammar is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{HybridResult}::={}&
\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}(\chi_T,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton})\\
&\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}
\mid\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\\
&\mid\operatorname{COND\_QE}(\chi_Q,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton}),
\end{split}
\tag{1}
\]
where each displayed \(\chi\) is a \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) and \(\mathsf{isSingleton}\) is the exact Boolean output of the associated closed first-order sentence.

The deterministic procedure \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) first runs \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).  A successful rational identification is returned as \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}\).  Every other terminal invokes the graph-compatible canonical fiber
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P).
\]
Every quantifier-elimination call below is made in the first-order language of real-closed fields with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\); its computation performs only exact coefficient operations in \(\mathbb D\), and its returned syntax is interpreted over \(\mathbb R\).  For \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\), apply quantifier elimination to
\[
\varphi_T(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{2}
\]
and denote the output by \(\chi_T(t)\).  Apply it to the closed sentence
\[
\exists t_1,t_2\,[\chi_T(t_1)\wedge\chi_T(t_2)\wedge t_1\ne t_2]
\tag{3}
\]
and to
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t],
\qquad
\chi_T(u)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow t\leq u]
\tag{4}
\]
to form the singleton Boolean and endpoint formulas.

For a conditional target put \(e=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\) and \(n=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf N:&\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0]
\ \wedge\ \exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0].
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Three quantifier-elimination calls yield closed quantifier-free formulas whose exact constant sign evaluations decide \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\).  The block in \((5)\) is also a reusable checked subroutine on any explicitly supplied nonempty canonical fiber obtained by replacing \(S\) in all three formulas; its zero, mixed, and positive meanings and its two payload-free terminal labels are unchanged.  The first two cases return the corresponding payload-free evidence terminals.  Only in case \(\mathsf P\) is quantifier elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_Q(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{6}
\]
to form \(\chi_Q(t)\), its singleton Boolean, and endpoint formulas as in \((3)\)--\((4)\).  The procedure returns formulas and decisions only: it returns no explicit endpoint value, algebraic sample, cylindrical algebraic decomposition trace, canonical parameter, or paired SCM.

Let \(\mathcal U\) be a finite set of physically realizable candidate experiments.  Each \(e\in\mathcal U\) discloses a finite block of complete typed output laws, including every cell of each declared finite output, whose probabilities are effectively rational or real algebraic, and has an effectively comparable cost \(c_e>0\).  For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), let \(\mathcal P_S\) be \(\mathcal P\) augmented by all complete output laws disclosed by experiments in \(S\), and define
\[

\]

Uniform zero evidence or mixed zero and positive evidence returns the corresponding payload-free status and leaves the numerical full-menu conditional arm-ranking benchmark undefined.  Only when \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\) holds define
\[
n_\rho(\vartheta)
=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star).
\]
For a subset \(S\), define its numerical possibly-optimal set only when \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) holds, by
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)
=\left\{\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}:
\exists\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ 
n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0\right\}.
\]
Set
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full},G}=\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U),
\qquad
f_G(S)=|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|-|\operatorname{PO}_G(S)|
\]
on positive subsets, and define the exact broad-model ex-post acquisition problem by
\[
\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full},G}.
\]
Thus the acquired full menu, rather than the unaugmented menu, is required to establish uniform conditional definability.
changed.reason: The base-menu positivity requirement incorrectly rules out experiments whose information establishes conditional definability. {"id":"def:hybrid-result-grammar","name":"Real-semantic quantifier-elimination hybrid terminal grammar","construction":"Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring generated by the finitely many supplied rational or real-algebraic output-cell probabilities.  Their stipulated effective presentations give exact arithmetic and sign comparison in \(\mathbb D\), and an order-preserving embedding \(\mathbb D\hookrightarrow\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) supplies exact coefficient representations.  A \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) is finite syntax for a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign tests with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\).  For every real-closed field \(K\) containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\), this syntax has the usual realization \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_K\) in its displayed free variables.  In particular, the causal realization used below is \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_{\mathbb R}\) over the ordinary real field; neither canonical probability variables nor free target-value variables are restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

The hybrid terminal grammar is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{HybridResult}::={}&
\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}(\chi_T,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton})\\
&\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}
\mid\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\\
&\mid\operatorname{COND\_QE}(\chi_Q,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton}),
\end{split}
\tag{1}
\]
where each displayed \(\chi\) is a \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) and \(\mathsf{isSingleton}\) is the exact Boolean output of the associated closed first-order sentence.

The deterministic procedure \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) first runs \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).  A successful rational identification is returned as \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}\).  Every other terminal invokes the graph-compatible canonical fiber
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P).
\]
Every quantifier-elimination call below is made in the first-order language of real-closed fields with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\); its computation performs only exact coefficient operations in \(\mathbb D\), and its returned syntax is interpreted over \(\mathbb R\).  For \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\), apply quantifier elimination to
\[
\varphi_T(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{2}
\]
and denote the output by \(\chi_T(t)\).  Apply it to the closed sentence
\[
\exists t_1,t_2\,[\chi_T(t_1)\wedge\chi_T(t_2)\wedge t_1\ne t_2]
\tag{3}
\]
and to
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t],
\qquad
\chi_T(u)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow t\leq u]
\tag{4}
\]
to form the singleton Boolean and endpoint formulas.

For a conditional target put \(e=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\) and \(n=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf N:&\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0]
\ \wedge\ \exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0].
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Three quantifier-elimination calls yield closed quantifier-free formulas whose exact constant sign evaluations decide \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\).  On any explicitly supplied nonempty canonical fiber, the single closed formula in \(\mathsf P\) is the reusable uniform-positivity decision; the full block in \((5)\) is used when a failed positivity screen must be classified as uniform zero or mixed zero and positive evidence.  The zero, mixed, and positive meanings and the two payload-free terminal labels are unchanged after replacing \(S\) consistently throughout the block.  The first two cases return the corresponding payload-free evidence terminals.  Only in case \(\mathsf P\) is quantifier elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_Q(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{6}
\]
to form \(\chi_Q(t)\), its singleton Boolean, and endpoint formulas as in \((3)\)--\((4)\).  The procedure returns formulas and decisions only: it returns no explicit endpoint value, algebraic sample, cylindrical algebraic decomposition trace, canonical parameter, or paired SCM.","free_symbols":["\mathsf{QEFormula}","\mathsf{HybridResult}","\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}","\mathsf{DCTFTR}","\mathscr R(\mathcal P)","\mathcal P","\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)","T","\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta)","E","B_\rho","\rho"],"inputs":["\mathcal P","\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)","\mathsf{DCTFTR}"]}
